title: Anion and Solvent Manipulated Out-to-In Growth Mechanism to Assemble a Series of Different Dysprosium Clusters

material_class.structural_family: discrete Dy9 cluster; two μ5-(L)4- ligands, one μ2-OH, six μ3-OH, twelve nitrate and three aqua ligands

synthesis.procedure: H4L was prepared by a reported method. Add 0.05 mmol (28 mg) H4L, 0.4 mmol Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (183 mg), 1.5 mL EtOH, 0.5 mL CH3CN and 0.15 mL triethylamine to a one-end-closed Pyrex tube about 25 cm long. After sonicating for 15 minutes, seal the tube, heat in an oven at 80 °C for three days, then slowly cool to room temperature to precipitate yellow lumpy crystals. Yield about 32.6% based on the ligand. Elemental analysis for C71H70Dy9N30O59: calcd C 22.69, H 1.88, N 10.99; found C 22.45, H 2.05, N 10.81.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature gave yellow lumpy crystals.

properties.summary: DC susceptibility (1000 Oe, 2–300 K) gives room-temperature χmT close to nine uncoupled Dy(III) ions and a low-temperature drop assigned to Stark-level depopulation and weak antiferromagnetic interactions. Magnetization at 2 K and 5 T is far below the free-ion value and indicates strong anisotropy; the 2 K hysteresis loop is not obvious. Zero-field AC data (1–999 Hz, 2–15 K) show frequency-dependent SMM behavior without a peak, attributed to fast quantum tunneling; Cole–Cole data were fit to Arrhenius relaxation.

material_class.structural_family: discrete Dy3 cluster; one (H2L)2- chelating three Dy(III), one μ3-OAc and six terminal acetates

synthesis.procedure: Add 0.05 mmol (28 mg) H4L, 0.4 mmol Dy(OAc)3·6H2O (180 mg), 1.5 mL EtOH, 0.5 mL CH3CN and 0.15 mL triethylamine to a one-end-closed Pyrex tube about 25 cm long. After sonicating for 15 minutes, seal the tube, heat at 80 °C for three days, then slowly cool to room temperature to give yellow lumpy crystals. Yield about 42.3% based on the ligand. Elemental analysis for C46H51Dy3N7O23: calcd C 35.66, H 3.32, N 6.33; found C 35.29, H 3.66, N 6.58.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature gave yellow lumpy crystals.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χmT is below the value for three uncoupled Dy(III) ions and falls on cooling, then rises at the lowest temperatures, which is attributed to intramolecular Dy–Dy exchange. Magnetization at 2 K and 5 T is unsaturated relative to the free-ion limit and anisotropic; hysteresis at 2 K is not obvious. Zero-field AC susceptibility shows frequency-dependent SMM behavior without a peak because of fast quantum tunneling.

material_class.structural_family: discrete grid-like Dy12 cluster of four vertex-sharing Dy3L units with a central cavity

synthesis.procedure: Add 0.05 mmol (28 mg) H4L, 0.4 mmol Dy(OAc)3·6H2O (180 mg), 1.5 mL CH3OH, 0.5 mL CH3CN and 0.15 mL triethylamine to a one-end-closed Pyrex tube about 25 cm long. After sonicating for 15 minutes, seal the tube, heat at 80 °C for three days, then slowly cool to room temperature to precipitate yellow long crystals. Yield about 48.9% based on the ligand. Elemental analysis for C156H144Dy12N24O72: calcd C 34.34, H 2.66, N 6.16; found C 34.02, H 2.93, N 6.38.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature gave yellow long crystals.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χmT is below the value expected for twelve uncoupled Dy(III) ions and decreases on cooling. Magnetization at 2 K and 5 T remains well below the free-ion limit, consistent with strong crystal-field anisotropy; 2 K hysteresis is not obvious. Zero-field AC data show frequency-dependent SMM relaxation without a peak. Under a 1500 Oe DC field, only cluster 3 shows field-induced SMM behavior with a higher Arrhenius barrier. Slow relaxation is ascribed mainly to single-ion Dy(III) anisotropy.
